## QUESTION 2

__What year had the most babies named 'David'? How many babies were named 'David' that year?__

The year that had the most babies born with the name "David" was: 1955
There were 86389 babies named "David" born in that year.

```{python}
# Q2

'''
I need to:
[x] only have rows where the name is David
[x] then add together the # born in each year (Which is already done in the data set as total)
[x] take the year with the most of them

[x] print the year and the number.
'''

answerA = df.filter(pl.col("name") == "David").sort("Total", descending=True)["year"][0]

answerB = df.filter(pl.col("name") == "David", "year").select("Total").max().item()


print(f'The year that had the most babies born with the name "David" was: {answerA}')
print(f'There were {answerB} babies named "David" born in that year.')

```


## QUESTION 3

__What year did your name hit its peak? How many babies were named your name in that year?__

My name (Justin) hit its peak in 1988
In that year there were 35243 babies born with my name.

```{python}
# Q3

answerA = df.filter(pl.col("name") == "Justin").sort("Total", descending=True)["year"][0]

answerB = df.filter(pl.col("name") == "Justin", "year").select("Total").max().item()

print(f'My name (Justin) hit its peak in {answerA}\nIn that year there were {answerB} babies born with my name.')

```


## QUESTION 4

__In the most recent year, what was the most common female name in Utah?__ 

In the dataset, the most recent year is 2024, and in that year, the most common female name in Utah is Olivia which was given to about 215 female babies.

```{python}
'''
- The provided dataset has no Sex column, so "female" saddly has to come from another dataset
  the names_prob dataset (has prob_female per name), joined to the
  per-year/per-state counts we already have in df.

[x] Find the .max of 'year'
[x] Get name + UT count for that year
[x] Join with names_prob to get prob_female
[x] Estimate female count = UT * prob_female
[x] Sort by highest estimate
[x] display the results
'''

names_prob = pl.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4names/master/data-raw/names_prob/names_prob.csv", infer_schema_length=None)

max_year = df.select(pl.col("year").max()).item()

df_new = df.filter(pl.col("year") == max_year).select("name", "UT")
df_new = df_new.join(names_prob.select("name", "prob_female"), on="name", how="left").drop_nulls()
df_new = df_new.with_columns((pl.col("UT") * pl.col("prob_female")).alias("female_estimate"))
df_new = df_new.sort("female_estimate", descending=True)

print(f'In the dataset, the most recent year is {max_year}, and in that year, the most common female name in Utah is {df_new.head(1)["name"].item()} which was given to about {round(df_new.head(1)["female_estimate"].item())} female babies.')

```
